new.title: Trace the Kaiserpfalz remains of Barbarossa
new.desc: Emperor Friedrich I Barbarossa had an imperial palace built here after 1152, which gave the city its name Kaiserslautern. Only foundation stones of the Kaisersaal and parts of the castle chapel survive beside the Casimirsaal.
new.tip: The outdoor area is freely accessible. Guided tours of the underground passages can be booked through the Tourist Information at Fruchthallstraße 14.

new.title: Step into the Gothic Stiftskirche
new.desc: The Stiftskirche is regarded as the most important late Gothic hall church in southwest Germany. It grew from a 9th-century chapel and the Premonstratensian foundation of the mid-12th century, supported by Barbarossa; its carillon rings several times a day.
new.tip: Open weekdays in the morning and early afternoon (shorter on Fridays), so check hours first. Concerts are held here.

new.title: See the Fritz-Walter-Stadion on the Betzenberg
new.desc: Home of 1. FC Kaiserslautern, the stadium sits on the Betzenberg and is named after the 1954 World Cup-winning captain Fritz Walter. A small Fritz-Walter-Museum belongs to the ground.
new.tip: The museum opens Sundays 12:00 to 16:00 and before home matches. Stadium tours are requested by email at stadionfuehrung@fck.de.

new.title: Stroll the Japanischer Garten and its torii
new.desc: Visitors enter this Japanese garden through a red torii gate. It has a teahouse where tea ceremonies take place and is known for its cherry blossom in spring.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday March to October, Friday to Sunday November to February. Go in April for the blossom.

new.title: Browse the mpk Museum Pfalzgalerie
new.desc: The Museum Pfalzgalerie, run by the Bezirksverband Pfalz, holds a permanent collection of art plus special exhibitions. It stands on Museumsplatz next to a small park.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; Thursday is open until 20:00. Combine it with the Pfalztheater five minutes away.

new.title: Climb the Humbergturm above the forest
new.desc: The observation tower on the Großer Humberg, about 424 m above sea level, is roughly 35 m high and reached by 163 stone steps. It looks over the city and the Palatinate Forest and is maintained by a local association.
new.tip: Open around the clock. It makes a good goal for a hike from the city.

new.title: Explore the Burg Hohenecken ruin
new.desc: This Hohenstaufen-era spur castle stands on the Schlossberg above the district of Hohenecken. It is first documented in 1277, when the lords who called themselves von Hohenecken were enfeoffed, and later became a Ganerbenburg.
new.tip: Reach it by train (RB 64 to Hohenecken) or bus 101 or 111 to Hohenecken, Burg. Guided tours can be booked through the castle website.

new.title: Admire the Fruchthalle from 1849
new.desc: The Fruchthalle was built in the mid-19th century to plans by August von Voit. The provisional Palatinate government met here in May 1849 during the revolution, and the building is a protected monument.
new.tip: Tours can be booked through the Tourist Information. Check events held inside.

new.title: Visit the Stadtmuseum in the Wadgasserhof
new.desc: The Stadtmuseum covers art and cultural history of the city across two historic buildings, the Theodor-Zink-Museum and the Wadgasserhof.
new.tip: Closed Monday and Tuesday; open Wednesday to Friday 10:00 to 17:00 and weekends 11:00 to 18:00.

new.title: Look out from the Schlachtenturm in Morlautern
new.desc: The lookout tower stands at about 327 m in Morlautern. It was built in 1893 to commemorate the 1793 battle fought on these hills.
new.tip: Free to approach; the tower stands in woodland, so wear sturdy shoes.

new.title: See the Pfalztheater on Willy-Brandt-Platz
new.desc: The Pfalztheater is the city's theatre, staging musical theatre, drama and ballet, plus a Junges Pfalztheater for young audiences.
new.tip: Check the programme and book tickets at the box office.

new.title: Watch the city from the Kleiner Humberg
new.desc: The Kleiner Humberg south of the centre gives views over Kaiserslautern and is popular for family hikes and picnics.
new.tip: Start from Wienertal and combine it with the Humbergturm.

new.title: Eat Saumagentaler in a 1742 half-timbered house
new.desc: Spinnrädl is a restaurant in what is described as the oldest standing half-timbered house in Kaiserslautern, dating to 1740 to 1742. It serves hearty Palatinate cooking.
new.tip: Try the Saumagentaler or the Wildgulasch with a glass of Pfälzer wine. Check the current menu and hours.

new.title: Drink house beer at the Brauhaus am Markt
new.desc: The Brauhaus am Markt is a brewpub and bistro next to the Stiftskirche with its own beer and a terrace on the market square.
new.tip: Order the house beer; the beer tower is a local favourite. Food reviews are mixed, so come mainly for the beer.

new.title: Dine at Melissa's Esszimmer
new.desc: Melissa's Esszimmer, formerly Weinhaus Stepp, is a fine-dining restaurant in the city centre. A Rheinpfalz review called it not cheap but worth every cent.
new.tip: Main courses are priced around 28 to 42 euros and set menus 63 to 82 euros. Open Tuesday to Saturday; book ahead.

new.title: Have regional Pfälzer cooking at Gasthof Fröhlich
new.desc: Gasthof Fröhlich in Dansenberg is a family-run inn with a restaurant serving traditional regional cuisine, a terrace and a beer garden.
new.tip: Ask for Pfälzer dishes such as Leberknödel or Saumagen and check the menu first. It lies away from the centre.
new.q: Gasthof Fröhlich, Dansenberger Straße 10, Dansenberg, 67661 Kaiserslautern

new.title: Order regional dishes and cake at Quack
new.desc: Quack is a relaxed spot with beer, German specialties and regional food, coffee and cake in the daytime and a breakfast menu in the morning.
new.tip: Come for breakfast or an afternoon slice of cake. Check opening hours.

new.title: Have breakfast at the Glockencafé
new.desc: Glockencafé is a café with coffee, cake, breakfast, organic and vegetarian dishes, wine and cocktails in the Innenstadt.
new.tip: Good for a brunch stop before the Stiftskirche; confirm current hours.

new.title: Sit in the beer garden of the Brauhaus
new.desc: The Brauhaus on Forellenstraße is listed as a traditional brewery restaurant with beer garden feel, regional cuisine and many beers.
new.tip: Pick the regional dish of the day; verify hours before going.

new.title: Swim and row on the Gelterswoog
new.desc: The Gelterswoog is the largest reservoir in the Palatinate Forest at about 11.5 ha, with lawns, a sandy beach and rowboat rental. Hiking loops of about 3 to 14 km start from the lake.
new.tip: Swimming is a summer activity. Bus 111 runs to Hohenecken, Gelterswoog.

new.title: Spend a day at the Gartenschau
new.desc: The Gartenschau grew out of the 2000 Landesgartenschau and is the city's largest park at about 14.8 ha, with a Dino-Park, playgrounds, a Weidenkirche and seasonal events.
new.tip: Open daily 9:00 to 19:00 from 23 March to 31 October. Entrance fees apply.

new.title: Walk through the Volkspark
new.desc: The Volkspark is the second largest park in the city at 8.8 ha, with lawns and paths close to the centre.
new.tip: Free and open all day; good for a picnic.

new.title: Visit the Zoo Kaiserslautern in Siegelbach
new.desc: The zoo, founded in 1968 as Tierpark Siegelbach and renamed in 2003, covers about 7 ha with roughly 500 animals from over 100 species. It has a tropical house, falconry and a nature trail.
new.tip: Open April to October 9:00 to 18:30, shorter hours in winter.
new.q: Zoo Kaiserslautern, Zum Tierpark 10, Siegelbach, 67661 Kaiserslautern

new.title: Go barefoot on the Barfußpfad
new.desc: The Barfußpfad is a barefoot path for children and adults to feel the forest floor and practise body awareness, with a barbecue spot nearby.
new.tip: Wear shoes you can take off easily. Best in dry weather.

new.title: See native animals in the Wildpark Betzenberg
new.desc: The Wildpark on the Betzenberg was founded in 1970 to show native animals, including some that no longer live wild nearby, along a forest walk.
new.tip: Free walk through woodland beside the stadium.

new.title: Catch a concert at the Kammgarn
new.desc: The Kulturzentrum Kammgarn is a cultural centre in a listed former textile mill. Its main hall holds about 1,000 standing guests and it hosts pop, rock, jazz, comedy and cabaret.
new.tip: Check the programme on the venue site, Eventim or Songkick.

new.title: Browse the farmers' market on Stiftsplatz
new.desc: The farmers' market takes place on Stiftsplatz in front of the Stiftskirche, early in the morning until about 13:00.
new.tip: Tuesdays and Saturdays are reported; the city says it moves between Stiftsplatz and Königstraße, so check the city site.

new.title: Hike a stage of the Pfälzer Waldpfad
new.desc: The Pfälzer Waldpfad is a premium hiking trail of about 140 km in nine stages through sandstone forest, ending at Schweigen-Rechtenbach on the Deutsche Weinstraße.
new.tip: Get maps at the Tourist Information, Fruchthallstraße 14.
